passes.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
EDIT the attached painted retro-futurist government time-travel station panorama. Keep the exact full 3:1 frame, camera, architecture, portal locations and scales, material palette and neutral lighting. ONE localized security-equipment addition only.

USER GOAL: Nobody should be able to casually walk into an unguarded portal. Make ALL FIVE portal platforms look like controlled, gated departure bays. Three downstairs, two upstairs. Show a believable physical access-control perimeter for each portal, not just a lonely ticket reader that can be walked around.

SECURITY DESIGN:
- Around each portal's existing floor plinth/landing, build a compact perimeter of thin dark graphite structural posts holding clear reinforced glass panels with very faint neutral-gray tint, about adult shoulder height, with opaque metal kickplates only at the bottom. Glass must read transparent so the portal and architecture stay clearly visible. Grounded late-20th-century industrial design upgraded with futuristic mechanics: bolted bases, recessed channels, modest worn brass joints, small ochre latch covers.
- At the public-facing front of EACH bay place ONE clearly CLOSED two-panel sliding security gate in the glass perimeter. Gate panels meet at a visible central seam and retract into side housings; no hole or unguarded opening around either side. Include a small physical card/passport reader with a dark screen mounted on a gatepost, plus an integrated latch. People would approach from the hall, authorize at the reader, enter the bay and then approach the ring. Entry gate positioned in FRONT of the ring landing, not a shutter in the portal aperture.
- Side panels and the rear edge must visibly connect into a coherent enclosed bay footprint, with a discreet closed staff/service panel integrated into one side. No loose disconnected barrier segments.
- The largest front-center portal gets the most readable bay, with adequate standing clearance between gate and ring. Its gate must connect to its perimeter and face the player. Render its posts and glass in the same perspective as the pale floor tiling. Avoid crowding the whole hall with barriers; stay near the existing portal zone.
- The two rear ground-floor portals retain the recently increased setback and same shared baseline, with matching smaller-scaled security bays. These two rings stay separately visible; do not merge them into one big enclosure.
- Give both upstairs portals matching scaled access-control gates behind the existing balcony railing. Preserve a wide pedestrian aisle between bay fronts and balcony railing; NOTHING crosses the skybridge path.
- Treat these as permanent functional station infrastructure with light wear, not temporary velvet queue ropes, construction fences, nightclub stanchions, prison bars or opaque cages. No spikes, guards, weapons, cameras everywhere, neon or forcefield.

STRICT INVARIANTS:
Do NOT move, resize or redesign any of the five portals, their bases or machinery. Do NOT put a new barrier across the entire foreground or window panorama. Keep all three lower-right corridor doorways and their approaches clear. Keep stairs/elevator access and left observation promenade clear. Keep the clock REMOVED and lower-right freestanding ticket machines REMOVED. Keep seating, vending machine, phone, bins, artifacts, lockers, banners, board and all repaired window framing unchanged. Do not extend the hall or generate a new city.
No people, desk, text, clock, extra kiosks, new walls, portal energy or glowing screens. Neutral diffuse painted art only; no baked directional sunlight, lamp pools or glowing security barriers. New glass reflections very restrained and untinted so dynamic lighting can be added later.
Preserve original scene and add well-integrated access-controlled portal bays with clean perspective, complete perimeter connectivity and sensible circulation.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
EDIT the supplied 2172x724 panoramic painted station artwork. This is a very localized DOOR AND SIGNAGE pass. Preserve the full frame, camera, exact architecture, all FIVE recently added transparent secure portal bays, all five portals, their positions, floor pattern, furniture, materials, lighting, city, windows, stairs and museum displays. Do not change or remove the security gates!

User says the signs beside the doors must correspond to each door, the doors should be closed, and the department symbols should have a funny representation.

TARGET: ONLY the THREE lower-level corridor doorways on the right wall, between the rear portal area and the display/bench area. From left (farthest away, near the rear portal) to right (closest to the artifacts), they are MEDBAY, DETENTION, EXECUTIVE SUITES. Those words are semantic descriptions ONLY: paint NO letters or words.

CLOSE all three doorways with properly fitted industrial double sliding door leaves, visible center seams, closed flush in the existing frames. The dark open corridors become closed solid door surfaces. Preserve original doorway dimensions and their wall perspective. Do not create another door or seal the elevator. Empty floor approach to every door; no kiosks, barriers, props in front.

Give each door ONE matching, clearly readable department pictogram sign directly centered above that doorway on its header, below its ventilation grille. Use the existing sign/header space, not floating signs or signs on the neighboring wall:
- Farthest/leftmost doorway: MEDBAY icon = a simple red heart with a cream diagonal bandage and one small repair wrench. The joke is treating people as repair jobs. Closed warm-gray door, a narrow muted oxblood identification stripe.
- Middle doorway: DETENTION icon = a simple cream stick-person head/body behind THREE vertical bars, holding one little blank queue ticket out between bars. Clear simple institutional icon, dry joke, not a detailed character illustration. Charcoal door with a small worn ochre identification strip.
- Closest/rightmost doorway: EXECUTIVE SUITES icon = an oversized upholstered office chair with a tiny crown above it, cream and brass silhouette on a restrained plum sign. Closed charcoal doors with modest worn brass trim.
Signs should be the same visual family and consistent physical size, scaled in perspective. Clean bold few-shape icons so they read at game resolution, no tiny detailed illustrations. All three icons attached to the correct individual door with no ambiguity. Replace/remove the misleading green running-man EXIT badges beside THESE THREE department doors only. Preserve actual emergency-exit pictograms at the staircase and elsewhere. Keep the fire-hose reel and safety equipment intact.

Style: worn institutional enamel pictograms, understated dystopian humor, no cartoons pasted over the scene, no modern flat UI overlay, no glowing signage. Avoid any letters, numbers, words, invented glyphs, slogans, labels. The game will supply department names and status text later.

Invariants: clock stays removed; free-standing ticket kiosks stay removed; front/rear/upstairs portal positions and transparent security bays stay exactly unchanged; no people or crowd added; city stays unchanged as placeholder one exterior layer. Neutral diffuse painted light; no baked sunlight, added glow or cast-light effects.
Return the same complete 3:1 panorama with only those three doors closed and department pictograms corrected.

Precise localized image edit. Image 1 is the 2172x724 EDIT TARGET. Return the complete SAME panorama. Change only the malformed emergency-exit sign at the FAR UPPER RIGHT of the hall, mounted above the upstairs seating/console near the right edge. Approximate region x2100–2150 y130–173 in the native canvas. It currently contains a malformed ambiguous white figure.

Replace that one sign with a crisply designed SIMPLE pictogram: one single ivory running person entering an outlined doorway, plus one bold RIGHT-POINTING arrow. One round head, one torso, exactly two bent arms, exactly two bent legs, no doubled bodies, no decorative squiggles, no lettering, no word EXIT. Strong clean geometric silhouette and adequate space between person and arrow. Standard clear visual language rather than ornate AI-generated symbols. A thin physical metal frame, matte dark muted green sign face, flat ivory graphics, realistic consistent wall perspective and modest physical size. You may make the plaque slightly wider (about 55x30 pixels on native image) to keep arrow and person clearly distinct. No glow or light pool.
Do not change any other signage: the three recently added lower-right department pictograms (bandaged heart; person/ticket/bars; crowned chair) stay unchanged, as do their CLOSED doors. The existing staircase signs stay untouched.
Do not alter architecture, windows, bridge, five empty portal rings or their SECURE glass access bays, portal positions, front/upper floor space, existing equipment, furniture, colors, city, camera or framing. No clock, ticket kiosks, crowds, desk, text, portal energy or additional decorations.
This is ONLY a legibility repair to the tiny upper-right emergency exit plaque. Preserve the rest of the image with maximum fidelity.
